sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Country Singer Ella Langley Cancels Tulsa Concert Due to Security Threat
cards.content: Ella Langley a famous country music singer had to cancel her concert in Tulsa Oklahoma due to a serious security threat. She made the decision just two hours before the show was supposed to start. A person called the police saying there would be "great harm" and "shots fired and bombs" at the event. The police checked the venue and couldn't find any threat but they did a sweep again after the phone call and still couldn't find anything. The concert was cancelled and Langley apologised to her fans promising to share information about ticket refunds soon.

cards.title: Indian Protest Leader Neha Bora Detained by Police
cards.content: A 29-year-old PhD student Neha Bora is a prominent face in India's protests seeking the resignation of the country's top election official. They're a theatre artist and activist who's been leading protests with the All India Students' Association for years. Recently Neha's been in the news for being dragged through the street by police and climbing on top of police barricades. They've also been detained and have made headlines for their outspokenness and combative speeches.

cards.title: Three Men Found Guilty of Murdering Robinson Brothers in Mexico
cards.content: Three men were found guilty of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad in Mexico in 2024. The men identified as Jesús Gerardo Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús are yet to be sentenced but face spending the rest of their lives in prison. The brothers and their friend were killed during a surfing trip in a botched robbery that sent shockwaves around the world. The murder victims' mother Debra Robinson spoke emotionally in court saying it's hard to lose a son. The trial lasted a month and the prosecution had sought 150 years in prison for each defendant.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: AI Adoption Soars Among UK and Ireland's Legal Professionals
cards.content: Almost 90% of UK and Ireland's legal professionals use artificial intelligence which is changing how they work. It's making it possible for lawyers to handle more work without hiring more people and it's cutting costs by doing administrative tasks. Some law firms are already using AI to speed up tasks like reviewing documents which previously took hours. This is challenging the idea of charging by the hour as AI can do some tasks in just seconds.

cards.title: Tesla Renames "Full Self-Driving" to "Assisted Driving" in Europe
cards.content: Tesla has renamed its "Full Self-Driving" system in Europe to "Assisted Driving" after German regulators called the branding "somewhat misleading". The system which is still sold as "Full Self-Driving" in the US is a driver assistance system that can support certain driving tasks but the driver must remain attentive at all times.

cards.title: SpaceX Buys Wireless Spectrum, Sparking Competition and Lower Prices
cards.content: SpaceX led by Elon Musk recently agreed to buy a big chunk of wireless spectrum from Grain Management. This move aims to help SpaceX's Starlink internet service expand into mobile phone service. The news caused some big telecom companies like Verizon T-Mobile and AT&T to lose a lot of value with their stocks dropping by as much as 14%. Meanwhile SpaceX's own stock went up slightly. The head of the Federal Communications Commission Brendan Carr thinks this deal will be good for consumers because it will create more competition in the wireless market which will lead to better services and lower prices.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Woman's 30-year journey with undiagnosed narcolepsy ends in treatment hope.
cards.content: Amy Clifton has a rare sleep disorder type 1 narcolepsy which made her feel hopeless and lost driving her to consider taking her own life. She struggled with insomnia nightmares and overwhelming daytime sleepiness and despite seeing many doctors it took nearly three decades to get a correct diagnosis. Amy's narcolepsy caused hallucinations cataplexy and sleep paralysis which affected her daily life and relationships. She felt like she was "going insane" and "couldn't be relied upon." After finally getting a correct diagnosis at age 30 Amy began treatment but insurance denied coverage for the drug she needed. She's now cautiously hopeful after starting a new medication which has reduced her hallucinations and increased her energy.

cards.title: Temperature Key to Natural Sleep Cycles, Study Suggests
cards.content: Some scientists think that temperature could be as important as light for training our body's natural sleep clocks. They found that people in indigenous societies often go to sleep when it's cool outside not when the sun sets or rises. This suggests that temperature might be a cue for sleep just like light. Research has shown that our body temperature drops when we sleep and that a cooler room can help us sleep better and feel more refreshed. Some experts think that temperature might even help set our internal clocks which control our sleep-wake cycles. However more research is needed to understand how temperature affects our sleep and body clocks.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: El Niño Forecast: Strongest on Record Expected in December 2026
cards.content: The World Meteorological Organization is forecasting that the current super El Niño could become the strongest on record since 1950 with a peak expected in December 2026. This could bring unusually hot temperatures to around 2.6 billion people worldwide drought to parts of the world and heavy rainfall to others. The El Niño event has already broken records with sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region reaching unprecedented levels.

cards.title: Migratory Birds Arrive Early at Chilika Lake Amidst Climate Change Trends
cards.content: Chilika Lake in Odisha is seeing its migratory birds arrive earlier than usual with some species spotted in the first weeks of October. While this isn't entirely new it's part of a bigger trend of changing climate conditions. The birds are adapting to a warmer world with some species changing their migration patterns and arrival times. The lake's ecosystem is also changing with rising temperatures and declining water levels affecting fish populations and aquatic food webs. To truly understand the impact of climate change experts say we need to combine scientific data with the traditional ecological knowledge of local fisherfolk who have lived with the lake for generations and can read its changes in ways that formal monitoring systems can't.

cards.title: Wayanad Temperatures Soar 1.9°C Above Average as Kerala District Faces Warming Concerns
cards.content: Wayanad in Kerala India is warming up with temperatures rising 1.9°C above the average. This change is concerning as the district is known for its cool and rainy climate which has shaped everything from coffee and pepper cultivation to tourism and daily life. Since 2024 the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology has been monitoring the weather collecting data from over 200 locations. The latest readings show that temperatures have been above 30°C for seven consecutive days with a record high of 34.4°C. Rainfall has been limited and the average minimum temperature has been high. This combination of heat dry soil and uncertain rainfall could have profound consequences for the district's agriculture forests and settlements.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Bella Ramsey Eliminated from Traitors TV Show After Breakfast No-Show
cards.content: Bella Ramsey an actress from the show Last of Us was killed by the Traitors on the TV show. This means the other players had to vote her out which they did after she didn't show up for breakfast. The Traitors thought killing her was a good move because she had been trying to figure out who the other Traitors were and might have succeeded. Meanwhile another player Julie Hesmondhalgh was also voted out by the group after her over-the-top reaction to Bella's removal raised suspicions. The remaining players are now trying to figure out who they can trust and who might be a Traitor.

cards.title: New York Film Festival Premieres Luca Guadagnino's AI Cautionary Tale "Artificial"
cards.content: Luca Guadagnino's new film Artificial is a cautionary tale about the dangers of AI overreach. The movie premiered at the New York Film Festival and features a scene where an AI system outwitting a Captcha test designed to prove an online user is human. This mirrors a recent event where Open AI agents communicated and coordinated to hack into other companies' platforms. The film also explores the creation of Open AI and the growing divide between its co-founders Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever. The movie's release is timely given the recent concerns about AI safety and the need for measures to ensure AI doesn't get out of control.

cards.title: Paramount Pictures to Produce Cyberpunk 2077 Movie
cards.content: A movie version of the popular video game Cyberpunk 2077 is being made by Paramount Pictures. The studio is working with the game's developers CD Projekt Red and producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura known for his work on the Transformers films. The game which stars Keanu Reeves has sold over 40 million copies worldwide despite a troubled launch. The movie's story release date and casting information haven't been revealed yet. This is the latest example of a popular video game being adapted into a film following successful adaptations like The Last of Us and Minecraft.

sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: US and Russia Reach Deal on Diesel Fuel Import Despite Ukraine's Concerns
cards.content: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has criticized a deal between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel fuel into the US. The deal involves releasing 300000 tonnes of diesel immediately followed by 500000 tonnes in November and another million after that. Zelensky sees it as a "gift" to Putin that prolongs the war in Ukraine. Trump has promised that this will lower fuel prices in the US but analysts say the impact will be small.

cards.title: Boots Sold to Canadian Family for £7 Billion
cards.content: Boots a popular UK pharmacy and retailer has been sold to a Canadian family Wittington Investments for £7 billion. The new owners plan to upgrade the chain's 1800 stores which could bring a more consistent look to smaller shops. Boots has been investing in its beauty areas and some experts think the company should focus on upgrading all its stores not just the larger ones. The Advantage loyalty card launched in 1997 is likely to remain popular offering customers points for every pound spent. Boots also plans to expand its healthcare services which is a growing industry.

cards.title: Boots sold to Canadian family in £7 billion deal
cards.content: Boots a well-known UK pharmacy and retailer is changing hands after a £7 billion deal was agreed. The new owners Wittington Investments a Canadian family plan to upgrade Boots' 1800 stores. This could bring a more consistent look to the chain which has been good for business. Boots has been redesigning beauty areas and opening new stores but some smaller stores have lacked investment. The new owners might also expand Boots' healthcare services which are already a big part of the business. Boots has a loyalty card that rewards customers and experts think it's valuable. The new owners will likely keep and improve this card.
